label: final copy step of length-3 sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, never during the original-token or delimiter steps. About 86% of activation mass is on the last step (t=5, outputting original token 2) of length-3 sequences. It fires on roughly 85% of those steps. The largest activations are on that step when the input (the echoed original token 1) is r or 3, e.g. c r o <DEL> c [r]. The rest is weak, scattered activity near the end of the copy phase in longer sequences (to_go 0-1, recall_idx 5-8), often on an input r that is not the first occurrence of that token. It is always off on first occurrences of the input token, so it never fires in the original phase. Adding the r clause raised mass recall to about 0.96 but cut precision a lot, so it was dropped.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: r, x, o, 3, y, p; least: z, 1, n, w) and the next token to output (most: c, t, q, -, z, w; least: d, h, k, b); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=5, L=3, t=5.
